MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY CGUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  AUGUST 12, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  - 6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to Order at 6:00 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins; and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein, and Steve Uhring.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 6:02 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Personnel Matters pursuant to Government Code Section 54957:

  Public Employee Performance Evaluation
  Title: City Manager

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins;  and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attomey; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Susan Duefias, Public
  Safety Director; Rob DuBouX, Public Works Director; Parker Davis, Media Technician;
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 12, 2024
  Page 2 of 15

  Christina Mufloz, Deputy City Clerk; Chris Orosz, Recreation Supervisor; and Raneika
  Brooks, Senior Planner

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Ranger Tim Pera led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 6:00 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54957, with all Councilmembers present He stated the Council discussed the items on the
  Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action.

  REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for this meeting was properly posted on
  August 2, 2024, with the amended agenda posted on August 9, 2024. She stated the
  amended agenda was properly posted in the posting board at City Hall, but the public may
  have an encountered an error accessing the agenda online over the weekend. She stated
  the staff reports for the meeting were available online over the weekend and a copy of the
  agenda was available online in the Public Meeting Video Archive.

  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The motion carried unanimously.

  ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Malibu Education Foundation Progress Update Presentation

  Karin Al—Hardan presented on progress establishing a centralized funding entity to
  help support Malibu schools.

  Daryl Adams, Malibu Middle School Athletic Coordinator, spoke about the Malibu
  Education Foundation athletic programs.

  Charlie Vanderbilt, Member of the Manta Rays soccer team, discussed his
  experience being part of the Founder’s Club and playing for the team.

  The Council directed questions to Ms. Al-Hardin, Stacy Rouse, and staff.

t  ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Norm Haynie discussed residents obtaining fire-flow water requirements in Lower
  Encinal Canyon. He discussed Water District No. 29 plans to remove the current
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 12, 2024
  Page 3 of 15

water tank t0 replace it with a larger tank. He expressed concern that Lower Encinal
Canyon would have insufficient water flow for fighting potential fires during the
proj ect.

Tim Pera, Mountains Recreation and Conservation Association (MRCA) Ranger,
provided the monthly coastal ranger report. He reported 299 parking citations, and
15 administrative citations were issued. He reported extended maintenance patrols
were implemented due to the high volume of visitors. He reported Los Angeles
County services were offered to an individual experiencing homelessness, and he
left Bluffs Park. He reported extended ranger patrols for fire prevention and
lookouts.

Kim Sichta deferred time to Joe Sichta.

Chris Ayotte deferred time to Joe Sichta.

Valerie Seabaugh deferred time to Joe Sichta.

Julia Morriss deferred time to Joe Sichta.

Joe Sichta, Malibu Aquatics Foundation, discussed the Malibu Aquatics
Foundation and the Malibu Seawolves swim team and changes in the swim program
and community over the last year. He discussed the replacement of Coach Eric
Rand, in part, due to his lack of ability to meet technical coaching needs and not
possessing U.S. Masters certification required for insurance. He requested review
of the request for qualifications (RFQ) process.

Sue Murphree deferred time to Patrick Murphree.

Patrick Murphree discussed his family’s participation in the Malibu Seawolves
swim program and the higher level of training received as opposed to the Malibu
High School swim club. He discussed his wife’s participation in the Malibu
Aquatics Foundation. He requested re-evaluation of the proposals to include
reviewers versed in U.S.A. swimming. He discussed the reduced pool time in the
selected proposal for older swimmers. He discussed the proposal reviewers.

Steve Hotchkiss discussed his involvement in founding the Malibu Seawolves
swim team and the Malibu Aquatics Foundation. He discussed coaching changes
and the swimming community and stated that the new swim club would not produce
a competitive swim team. He discussed the proposal reviewers.

Michel Shane discussed his Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) driver safety education
initiative which included working with children early on so they would be prepared
once they started driving.

Lester Tobias discussed the proposal he sent to City Council to improve the
planning development process. He encouraged City Council candidates to state if
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August l2, 2024
  Page 4 of 15

  they were in favor of fixing the planning process and suggested hiring him t0 fix it.
  He elaborated on his qualifications and ideas.

  Debra Bianco announced the Malibu Farmers Market 25th anniversary. She offered
  to sponsor a booth for the Malibu Aquatics Foundation. She requested the City
  allow the Farmer’s Market to use the perimeter of Legacy Park for the market.

  Ingrid Yael thanked Congressman Brad Sherman for awarding the Malibu Farmer’s
  Market and Cornucopia Foundation a certificate for outstanding and invaluable
  service to the community.

  Ryan Embree stated that he was pleased that the City was embarking on an update
  to the safety element of the General Plan. He discussed his attendance at a
  workshop hosted by Caltrans. He stated that the center lane was the emergency
  evacuation route and should not be removed.

  Bob Archer discussed Councilmembers Uhring and Silverstein, and Flaming
  Commission Chair Mazza’s relationship with the Malibu Township Council, and
  the treatment of staff, leading to turnover and costly litigation. He discussed delays
  in the planning process. He discussed postings on social media and unregistered
  lobbying activities.

  Kraig Hill discussed PCH safety and stated that the two applications for
  establishments that serve alcohol that were approved at the July 15, 2024 Flaming
  Commission meeting were at odds with the goal of improving safety. He discussed
  Land Use Policy 73 which limits the city to no more than one off—sale Alcoholic
  Beverage Control license per 2,000 residents and Land Use Policy 4.1.5 which
  prohibits undue concentration of businesses that sell alcohol for offsite
  consumption. He suggested that the Council publicly state the prioritization of
  safety, providing informal guidance for the Planning Commission. He suggested
  supporting businesses that do not detrimentally affect PCH safety and not promote
  Malibu as a drinking destination.

  Colin Drummond protested the aquatics program RFQ process and decision. He
  expressed concern regarding the selection process and merit of the evaluators. He
  stated the applicant that was selected would not serve the needs of the
  professionally aspiring swim community.

  Jo Drummond discussed PCH safety and requested a discussion item on Nobu’s
  conditional use permit (CUP) due to repeated violations. She stated that she spoke
  to Stacy Rouse ofthe Malibu Education Foundation and requested Melanie Haseker
  step down from the board due to her lack of fundraising experience and
  x.  responsiveness to inquiries, reinstate Karin Al—Harden as president, scale back
M
  board membership, and conduct open meetings. She discussed the skate park
  design and suggested it be kept competitive and challenging.

  Bill Sampson discussed his sobriety and the Flaming Commission meeting where
   Malibu City Council
  Minutés of August 12, 2024
  Page 5 of 15

  the applications fOr alcohol sale were approved. He discussed his participation in
  the masters swim program. He discussed the flawed selection process for the swim
  program.

  Kai Mizumo discussed Councilmember Silverstein’s interest in exposing
  corruption and requested he examine Councilmember Uhring’s and Flaming
  Commission Chair Mazza’s activities that he felt were improper.

  ITEM 2.13.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  City Manager McClary discussed Nobu and stated that they were cited for an
  unpermitted event on July 4, 2024. He stated that Nobu management was urged to
  move forward with a conditional use permit (CUP) modification application. He
  stated that there would be an item on the potential modification or revocation of the
  existing CUP. He discussed the Topanga Lagoon Restoration proj ect and stated the
  public comment period ends August 13, 2024. He reported LAZ parking
  enforcement started July 4, 2024, issuing 2,135 of the more than 4,000 parking
  citations issued in the City. He thanked those who participated in phase one of the
  Malibu Community Lands outreach project and announced the second workshop
  would be held at 6:00 p.m. on August 22, 2024, at City Hall. He stated that Senate
  Bill 1297 pertaining to speed cameras was scheduled to go to the assembly
m  appropriations committee during the current week, and, if approved, would proceed
  to the assembly floor for a vote. He pro'vided CHP PCH statistics for the period of
a- J
  January through mid-July 2024. He reported nearly 1,800 speeding tickets were
  issued, three for over 100 mph, and one for reckless driving. He reported six
  vehicles were impounded, six arrests for offenses not related to driving under the
  influence (DUI), and three arrests for DUI. He stated nearly 2,100 citations total
  were issued during that period. He announced an in—person Caltrans PCH master
  plan community workshop was scheduled for August 28, 2024, from 6:00 p.m. to
  8:00 pm. at City Hall. He stated a Virtual workshop would be held September 12,
  2024. He announced the City’s Safety and Preparedness Fair was scheduled for
  September 15, 2024.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, provided
  statistics for July 2024. He reported 47 part one crimes, which brought the year—
  to-date total to 215, compared to 272 the prior year at the same time. He reported a
  citation was issued to a driver at Webb Way and PCH for speeding at 80 miles per
  hour in a 30 miles per hour zone. He reported the Beaches and Harbors
  maintenance complex at Zuma Beach was burglarized. He reported an arrest was
  made of an individual for possession of a loaded firearm at PCH and Serra Road.
  He reported an individual was arrested for DUI in the 22000 block of PCH. He
  reported an arrest was made in the 19000 block of PCH for possession of a stolen
  vehicle. He reported an arrest was made in the 31000 block of Broad Beach Road
  for possession of a stolen vehicle. He reported the beach team, through the end of
  July, issued 287 citations for alcohol on the beach, 303 traffic citations, 1,325
  parking citations, and 184 vehicles were towed. He reported the special assignment
  deputies, on August 8, 2024, at PCH and Carbon Canyon Road arrested an
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 12, 2024
  Page 6 0f 15

  individual who had two outstanding warrants for grand thoft and ovading police,
  for multiple offences. He reported that on August 9, 2024, the special assignment
  deputies, in the area of Tuna Canyon and PCH, arrested an individual for
  trespassing into a house that was for sale, and possession of property that was stolen
  on June 7, 2024, from a vehicle parked at Latigo Point.

  In response to Mayor Stewart, he stated that the area where many recreational
  vehicles parked along PCH, south ofTopanga Canyon Road, was the responsibility
  of the California Highway Patrol.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Uhring diSCussed his activities during the summer recess. He
  discussed a black bear on Harbor Vista Drive and the Los Angeles County Sheriff
  and Fish and Wildlife response to tag and relocate the bear. He stated he attended
  an event with a presentation of a large animal sling for use by the fire department
  for large animal rescue. He discussed the goats brush clearing event in the Malibu
  West neighborhood, and commended Tracy Weirick for her work on the event. He
  addressed the public speakers and discussed the letter from Adrian Fernandez.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, City Manager McClary stated the
  investigation into the allegations in the letter was underway.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed short-term rentals (STR) negotiations between
  the California Coastal Commission and the City of Seal Beach and the higher
  concentration of STRs in Malibu than Seal Beach. He discussed the need for a
  disaster fund and requested City Manager McClary provide more information. He
  recommended a commendation for the Malibu Farmers Market for their 25—year
  anniversary. He discussed the future Interim Planning Director and requested
  changes to Planning Department staff recommendations. He commented on the
  number of variances requested and granted. He discussed issues related to camps
  set up by individuals experiencing homelessness and requested action be taken.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, Assistant City Manager Toney stated staff
  was not providing direction or pushing projects forward, he stated staff frequently
  “said no” to
  proj ects daily and tried to help facilitate proj ects within the City’s code.

  Councilmember Grisanti stated his neighborhood had the running ofthe goats event
  and recommended goats for brush clearance. He discussed CCC permitting STRs
  in beach communities, and noted Seal Beach increased STR permits in the coastal
  zone and Malibu strived to reduce the number. In response to Ms. Drummond, he
  stated that the changes in the Skate Park design would not result in a less
  challenging course, but would be dug in deeper, with the drops remaining the same.
  He stated that he attended the CCC meeting the week prior, where they adopted the
  new sea rise guidance. He stated he went to the Los Angeles County Office of
  Education (LACOE) meeting on City’s petition, and announced the hearing will be
  scheduled for November 2024. He discussed Community Emergency Response
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 12, 2024
  Page 7 0f 15

  Team (CERT) restocking emergency supplies. He thanked Mr. Shane for
  participating in hearings in Sacramento regarding highway safety.

  Councilmember Silverstein thanked the public speakers and those who submitted
  written comments. He suggested written comments be sent in time for the
  Councilmembers to read them. In response to Mr. Haynie, he requested research
  on whether there would be water available for firefighting during the replacement
  of the water tank in Lower Encinal Canyon.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated staff had confirmation from USA swim that the Malibu Marlins team and
  coaches were in good standing and there was adequate liability insurance. She
  stated that the Marlins were going to do adult conditioning during the fall, so the
  Master swimming certification was not required. She stated it was staffs
  understanding that coach Eric Ran was a lifeguard at Malibu High School, and she
  did not know if he provided other services. She stated Malibu Marlins notified staff
  the organization was not a party in any litigation.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Mr. Sichta stated sharing the pool had
  allowed both teams to have swim time, but the water polo team was coming back
  and limiting available pool time. He stated Seawolves was not in support of sharing
 j
  the pool but accommodated the changes. He stated the program was willing to
  share the pool if possible.
L;
  Councilmember Silverstein, in response to Mr. Shane, commented on Cruise
  Malibu, and stated that the image of driving and seeing celebrities was not one he
  would like to see projected. He indicated support for Mr. Shane’s highway safety
  programs. He stated the Councilmembers were committed to improving the
  Flaming process and indicated support for a more expeditious review of small to
  medium proj ects, and tighter review of large and commercial proj ects. He indicated
  support for Farmers Market commendation. He suggested the location behind La
  Paz for a larger Farmers Market. He encouraged Mr. Archer and Mr. Mizumo to
  reach out to him directly with facts. He discussed correspondence from attorneys
  representing the Malibu Inn Motel proj ect that requested it to be remanded to the
  Flaming Commission or the Flaming Department.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated that
  the proj ect would require a separate public hearing.

  Councilmember Silverstein requested the Malibu Inn Motel applicant provide proof
  that the project was withdrawn by the applicant prior to the Council’s vote. He
  stated that since a resolution denying the project had not been presented to the
  Council for final approval, the applicant could withdraw the application, but the
  proj ect would not be remanded to the Flaming Commission. He stated that he was
  visited by the bear on Harbor Vista and he would hope that the bear would be
  relocated to someplace safe from the dangers people and PCH presented to her.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 12, 2024
  Page 8 of 15

Mayor Pro Tern Riggins stated she attended a LACOE meeting where the dates
were set for November hearings. She stated that there would be hearings by the
Santa Monica—Malibu Unified School District (SM-MUSD) on the agreement in
October. She announced the weed pulling event at Point Dume Headlands on
Wednesday, August 14, 2024. She announced she attended 49th annual Natural
Hazard Conference in Colorado and discussed Los Angeles County/Malibu fire
brigade program. She commented on the Seal Beach short term rentals and stated
that there were likely more hotel and motel accommodations in their community
than in Malibu. She encouraged Ranger Pera to contact the City’s Public Safety
Department for information on arson watch. She cemented on the challenges of
development in Malibu due to the comprehensive General Plan, Malibu Municipal
Code, and Local Coastal Program that strives to protect the environment. She
agreed there should be some streamlining, but it would take an in-depth analysis of
the variety of projects proposed.

In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, City Manager McClary stated that
regarding Encinal Canyon residents water issues they were experiencing, he spoke
with the building official geological team had issued corrections about four months
ago and had several meetings to clarify, and they were waiting for a resubmission.

Mayor Pro Tem Riggins announced the next Library Speaker series event on
August 13, 2024.

Mayor Stewart congratulated Tom Schaar on his silver medal in skateboard at the
2024 Olympics. He stated SM-MUSD had found a school bus solution for the first
semester. He commended Councilmember Grisanti, Councilmember Riggins and
the school district separation team for their work on school' district separation. He
discussed the community land outreach projected and encouraged the public to
participate in phase 2. He announced the speed camera bill would go before the
appropriations committee on August 15, 2024. He discussed the efforts from City
staff, community members, and legislators to get the speed camera bill approved.
He discussed the 4.4 earthquake today and thanked the Community Emergency
Response Team (CERT) for keeping the emergency bins supplied. He reminded
the public to prepare their emergency supplies. He discussed how the bear on
Harbor Vista had traveled from Claremont to Malibu. He stated there had not been
any maj or design changes to the skatepark. He stated on July 15, 2024 he attended
a City Council Policy Review Ad Hoc Committee meeting. He discussed options
to expedite small projects. He stated on Julyl 1, 2024 he spoke with the City’s
auditors. He stated he attended the Caltrans Feasibility Study meeting on July 18,
2024, and the Special City Council meeting on July 22, 2024, Malibu Business
Roundtable on August 2, 2024. He stated he participated in an interview for a
potential Interim Planning Director with Councilmember Riggins. He stated he had
a call with City Manager McClary, Public Safety Director Duenas, Councilmember
Silverstein, Captain Seetoo, and Seargent Soderlund to discuss PCH Safety. He
discussed understaffmg in the Sheriff’s Department and the importance of using
technology as a force-multiplier. He congratulated the candidates who are running
for City Council.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 12, 2024
  Page 9 of 15

  Interim City Attorney Rusin cautioned the, Councilmembers that they could not
  comment on individuals running for City Council.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Item Nos. 3.B.14 was pulled by the Council.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a
  motion to approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos. 3.B.14. The motion
  carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  1.  Second Reading and Adoption of Ordinance No. 520
  Recommended Action: Conduct second reading, unless waived, and adopt
  Ordinance No. 520, finding the proposed code amendments exempt under
  CEQA, approving the California Coastal Commission (CCC) suggested
  modifications to LCPA No. 20-001, an amendment to the LCP Local
  Implementation Plan (LIP) sign regulations, and repealing Ordinance No.
  483.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Waive Further Reading
  Recommended Action: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive full
  reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/or second reading and adoption.
  Approve Warrants
  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers
  72943-73199 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant
  Register No. 751 in the amount of the warrant appearing opposite their
  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $5,352,617.49. City of Malibu payroll check number 5479—5480 and
  ACH deposits were issued in the amount of $1,791,419.81.
  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the June 10, 2024 Regular
  Meeting and June 20, 2024 Special Meeting.
  Jake Kurediian Citizenship Award
  Recommended Action: At the recommendation of the Parks and Recreation
  Commission, approve the nominations of Shari Latta and Poison Free
  Malibu as the 2024 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award recipients.
  General Plan Safety Element Update
  Recommended Action: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 24—41 initiating
  amendments to the Safety Element of the General Plan and finding the
  action exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act; 2) Direct the
  Planning Commission to schedule a public hearing; and 3) Authorize the
  Mayor to execute a professional services agreement with Capstone City
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 12, 2024
  Page 10 of 15

  Flaming to assist Public Safety staff with securing and managing a
  consultant to update the Safety Element of the General Plan.
  Professional Services Agreements for On-Call Civil Engineering Services
  Recommended Action: l) Authorize the Mayor to execute Professional
  Services Agreements with Kimley—Horn & Associates, Inc. (Kimley-Horn),
  M6 Consulting, Inc. (M6), and Interwest Consulting Group (Interwest) to
  provide On-Call Civil Engineering Services.
  Professional Services Agreement for On—Call Traffic Engineering Services
  Recommended Action: 1) Authorize the Mayor to execute Professional
  Services Agreements with Kimely-Horn & Associates, Inc. (Kimley-Horn),
  Transtech Engineers, Inc., and General Technologies and Solutions (GTS)
  to provide On-Call Traffic Engineering Services.
  Professional Services Agreement for On-Call Land Surveying Services
  Recommended Action: 1) Authorize the Mayor to execute a Professional
  Services Agreement with MNS Engineers, Inc. to provide On—Call Land
  Surveying Services.
  Amendment to Professional Services with American Guard Services, Inc.
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 2
  to the Professional Services Agreement with American Guard Services, Inc.
  extending the term of the Agreement to expire July 8, 2025.
  10.  Los Angeles County Measure R Transportation Funding Agreement
  Amendment
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute‘the Los Angeles
  County Measure R Funding Agreement Amendment for the Pacific Coast
  Highway Median Improvements Proj ect.
  ll.  Malibu Education Foundation Memorandum ofUnderstanding Amendment
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. l
  to the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the City and the
  Malibu Education Foundation (MEF) for a General Fund Grant.
  12.  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the Existence of a Local
  Emergency Regarding Conditions on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH)
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24-40 extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency related to the increase of
  reckless and illegal driving on pacific coast highway and directing staff to
  coordinate efforts with other governmental agencies to increase attention
  and create programs to reduce the risk and danger associated with pacific
  coast highway in the City.
  13.  Investment Report for the Month Ending June 30, 2024
  Recommended Action: Receive the Investment Report for the month ending
  June 30, 2024.

The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  14.  Adoption of Resolution No. 24-43, Appointment and Employment Contract
  for Interim Flaming Director
  Recommended Action: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 24-43 appointing Maureen
  Tamuri as Interim Planning Director pursuant to Government Code Section
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes 0f August 12, 2024
  Page 11 of 15

  21221(h); and 2) Authorize the City Manager to execute the employment
  agreement with Maureen Tamuri.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded a
  motion to: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 24-43 appointing Maureen Tamuri as
  Interim Flaming Director pursuant t0 Government Code Section 2122l(h);
  and 2) Authorize the City Manager to execute the employment agreement
  with Maureen Tamuri. The motion carried unanimously.
